options.product: Microsoft Entra External ID - external tenant
options.plan: Basic MAU; customer-organization entitlement and billing unverified
options.region: No tenant region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Standard external tenant; CIAM; app-owned org/membership model unverified; no workforce guests, Graph bridge or SCIM

conditions: Limit this proposal to business-customer authentication in a standard external tenant with registered applications and customer sign-up/sign-in user flows. SUPPORTED is application-type context, not native customer-organization membership, resource isolation or full B2B readiness.

The external directory stores customer accounts and is separate from a workforce tenant. Define and review application-owned customer organization IDs, admissions and resource permissions before using login for SaaS tenant access.

Basic MAU allowance is not verified account entitlement, production capacity or a zero-cost guarantee. Cloud sources are mutable and dated, not release-pinned; no account, subscription or live application integration was created.
This organization-context scope does not inherit OIDC/SAML, public-client, workforce-broker, SCIM, group synchronization, controls or residency assertions from other Entra drafts.

evidence.summary: The external-tenant overview explicitly targets consumer and business-customer apps with a customer directory and user flows. Proposed SUPPORTED covers that application category only; customer organization and membership boundaries remain separate unresolved proposals.

conditions: The documented Invite external user preview is for administration, not customer sign-in to CIAM apps, and is incompatible with customer user flows. Do not use tenant-admin guest invitations as partner enrollment or application organization membership.

The general table at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers mentions invitations, but its authentication section and the admin guide restrict this path. Preserve that distinction rather than promoting the broad wording to portal support.

UNKNOWN remains until an application-owned partner admission, trusted organization mapping and scoped business-admin workflow are specified and verified. It does not mean every possible custom portal or invitation implementation is unsupported.

A partner business-admin role is not an Entra directory administrator or AuthWeave catalog-curator authority. No directory roles, Graph grants, invitation emails or privileged membership operations were performed.

evidence.summary: The external-tenant admin guide limits guest invitations to administration and explicitly excludes customer CIAM user flows. That boundary does not establish a customer partner-portal admission or membership model, so the selected application context stays UNKNOWN rather than UNSUPPORTED.

conditions: One external identity directory is not one SaaS customer organization. Directory tenant IDs, branding, email domains and self-entered attributes must not become authority for access to a customer's application resources.

External-tenant app registrations use single-directory accounts per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers. That account type is not evidence that application multi-tenancy is unsupported; workforce any-directory registration, cross-tenant synchronization and multitenant organizations are outside this scope.

Review the actual external-tenant token profile using https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/id-token-claims-reference: tid identifies the sign-in directory, not an application customer organization. Validate tokens and bind a stable directory-scoped user to an application-owned organization; generic common-endpoint examples are not the selected CIAM authority.

UNKNOWN remains until organization mapping, tenant selection and resource authorization are defined and tested. Reject missing, foreign or unknown context and failed switches without retaining old tenant permissions; no live tenant isolation or database enforcement was verified.

evidence.summary: The tenant guide distinguishes an external CIAM directory from workforce collaboration. It does not define the selected application's multiple customer-organization boundary; proposed UNKNOWN avoids conflating identity-directory tenancy with SaaS resource authorization.

conditions: Security-group CRUD, group memberships and app-role assignments are documented, but an explicit customer-organization model and its multiple-membership lifecycle are not established for this configuration. UNKNOWN is not absence of all group or membership APIs.

Application roles are application-specific and groups are directory-scoped per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/how-to-use-app-roles-customers. Neither a role nor membership in several security groups automatically proves membership in several business organizations.

The support table limits group app-role assignment and adding group claims to Microsoft Graph, while the RBAC guide shows admin-center procedures. Reconcile these paths with the deployed tenant before approval; no Graph bridge, permissions grant or verified group-claim completeness is selected.

Choose a trusted directory-scoped user key, not email or idp-based cross-tenant identity linking; app-specific sub values are not interchangeable across registrations. Define membership status, roles, admission, removal and cached JWT/local-session enforcement separately.

No membership changes, identity linking, invitations or offboarding acceptance were tested. App-owned mappings remain unverified and do not inherit native inbound SCIM, GROUP_SYNC or workforce guest lifecycle claims.

evidence.summary: The external-tenant support table documents group and role management, including Graph-only paths. Those primitives do not establish the selected application's customer-organization memberships, admission or lifecycle enforcement; the compatibility proposal remains UNKNOWN.
